targets.title: The Bell state is entangled while its local density is maximally mixed
targets.difficulty_rationale: Combines a general entanglement theorem with an explicit finite partial trace calculation involving square roots and complex conjugation. Author estimate only; neither domain difficulty nor Lean/API effort has been calibrated on models.
capabilities: Distinguish joint entanglement from locally mixed statistics
Compute a partial trace with explicit normalization
Control basis ordering in a tensor product
targets.statement: The canonical two-qubit Bell ket is entangled and its left marginal is I/2.
assumptions: Ket.MES Qubit is the normalized all-positive maximally entangled ket.
targets.physical_scope: The Bell state (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2); partial trace removes the right factor and yields the left qubit state.

provenance.note: The chosen MES has positive equal diagonal amplitudes.
Partial trace sums the right-factor diagonal blocks.
Author-hosted mathematical background; exact formal claim follows the pinned source and the displayed assumptions.

targets.target_source:
import QuantumInfo.States.Pure.Qubit

open scoped Matrix
open ComplexConjugate
open BigOperators

theorem physics_target  : (Ket.MES Qubit).IsEntangled ∧
    (MState.pure (Ket.MES Qubit)).traceRight.m =
      (1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 : Matrix Qubit Qubit ℂ) := by
  sorry
targets.reference_outline: Distinguish joint entanglement from locally mixed statistics; Compute a partial trace with explicit normalization; Control basis ordering in a tensor product.

known_shortcuts.note: Directly proves entanglement; the maximally mixed marginal still requires a matrix calculation.
The specialized tactic can automate much of the finite partial trace calculation.

limitations: All Hilbert spaces are finite dimensional over complex numbers with a fixed orthonormal basis; no continuum, unbounded operators, or approximation errors are modeled.

targets.title: Damped oscillator energy never increases
targets.difficulty_rationale: Provisional author estimate; no live calibration. Physical reasoning combines dissipation with a global argument; Lean work includes rational normalization and the mean-value API.
capabilities: derive the dissipative energy rate from the ODE
lift a derivative sign to a global order property
targets.statement: Every global differentiable solution of q̇ = v and m v̇ = −kq − γv has antitone mechanical energy.
assumptions: The two HasDerivAt equations hold at every real time.
targets.physical_scope: Unforced scalar viscously damped harmonic oscillator on all ℝ. The theorem is conditional on a global solution.

provenance.note: Exact monotonicity is a formal refinement of the stated loss of oscillator energy.

targets.target_source:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

theorem classical_target (q v : ℝ → ℝ) (m k γ : ℝ) (hm : 0 < m) (hk : 0 < k) (hγ : 0 ≤ γ)
    (hq : ∀ t, HasDerivAt q (v t) t)
    (hv : ∀ t, HasDerivAt v ((-k * q t - γ * v t) / m) t) :
    Antitone (fun t => m / 2 * (v t)^2 + k / 2 * (q t)^2) := by
  sorry
targets.reference_outline: derive the dissipative energy rate from the ODE; lift a derivative sign to a global order property

known_shortcuts.note: Mean-value theorem supplies global monotonicity after the energy rate is proved.
